Bifunctional Phosphonium Salt-catalyzed Enantioselective [4 + 2]
Annulation of Isoindigos with Allenes: Access to Complex
Heter ocycles with Centerpiece of 4H-Pyrans
Juan Du,
a
Jia-Hong W u,

Abstract: Structurally fused heterocycles encom-
passing 4H-pyran centerpiece are prevalent scaf-
folds with promising biological activities, but have
daunting synthetic challenges. Herein, we presented
a regio- and stereoselective [4 + 2] annulation of
isoindigo derivatives with allenes by bifunctional
phosphonium catalysis. This protocol provides a
complementary way for accessing complex hetero-
cyclic compounds.
Keywords: complex heterocycles; 4H-pyran deriva-
tives; [4 + 2] annulation; bifunctional phosphonium
salts; H-bonding interaction
Over the past decades, asymmetric phase-transfer
catalysis (PTC) has been recognized as a promising
and eff icient candidate for the enantioselective con-
struction of structurally diverse and synthetically
useful molecular architectures, and quaternary
ammonium salt catalysis has already been extensively
investigated as a powerful tool for asymmetric
transformations.
[1]
In contrast, even though two semi-
nal reports on phosphonium salt-catalyzed reactions
can be traced back to 1990s,
[2,3]
the field of
phosphonium salt catalysis was dormant thereafter for
nearly one decade. Until recently , the key break-
throughs were communicated by Ooi
[4a]
and
Maruoka,
[5a]
which refueled the field and led to the
renaissance of phosphonium salt catalysis.
[6]
The past
decade witnessed the significant advancement of
asymmetric phosphonium salt catalysis, which were
mainly contributed by four leading research groups of
Ooi,
[4]
Maruoka,
[5]
Ma,
[7]
and Zhao.
[8]
Numerous
phosphonium salt-catalyzed asymmetric transforma-
tions have been extensively studied, and the reaction
scope is mainly focused on conjugate addition,
Mannich reaction and substitution reaction. However ,
the phosphonium salt-promoted annulation reactions
are rare, despite such reaction process is a powerful
and versatile tool for the enantioselective synthesis of
both carbocyclic and heterocyclic compounds. T o the
best of our knowledge, just few examples on the
creation of chiral carbocyclic systems via annulation
processes under amino acid-derived phosphonium salt
catalysis were disclosed by Zhao and co-workers.
[8j–m]
Quite recently , we developed novel dipeptide-based
bifunctional phosphonium salt catalysts that were
successfully applied in enantioselective annulation
reactions and constructing a kaleidoscope of chiral
cyclic molecules.
[9]
Notably , such dipeptide-derived
phosphonium salts possess remarkably high tunability ,
but their utilizations in creation of chiral cyclic systems
have not been investigated in depth.
On the other hand, six-membered 4H-pyran hetero-
cycles are frequently encountered as privileged struc-
tural frameworks in numerous natural products and
pharmaceuticals because of their promising biological
activities (Figure 1). Among many 4H-pyran cores,
structurally fused and spirocyclic 4H-pyrans bearing
an all-carbon quaternary stereocenter at the pyran-
cycle are much attractive, and a number of [4 + 2]
annulations with commonly employing α,β-unsaturated
ketones as C4-synthons were reported as efficient
ways for affording such 4H-pyran systems.
[1 1,12]
Quite
recently , our group disclosed a highly enantioselective
formal [4 + 2] annulation between electron-deficient

allenes and 3-alkenyl-oxindoles by bifunctional
phosphonium salt catalysis, thus leading to facile
construction of chiral heterocyclic compounds bearing
4H-pyran core.
[9f]
However , structurally complex heter-
ocyclic architectures with a centrepiece of 4H-pyran
still remain to be hardly available from a synthetic
perspective. V irtually , such synthetic challenges faced
are intrinsic: firstly , the highly crowed nature of multi-
substituted alkenones makes the addition of C2-
substrates extremely dif ficult; secondly , how to control
the regioselectivity is another daunting challenge;
additionally , how to regulate the reactivity of alle-
noates under PTC conditions
[13]
also needs to be
solved. T o expand the scope of application of this
method and make the products more diverse in
structure, we herein wish to update a highly enantiose-
lective synthetic approach with employing an isoindigo
as a starting substance, via phosphonium salt-catalyzed
[4 + 2] annulation with allene, and thus lead to a
variety of optically pure, structurally fused and
spirocyclic 4H-pyran derivatives bearing a quaternary
stereocenter (Scheme 1).
W e began our investigation of [4 + 2] annulation
between model subtrate N-Boc isoindigo 1 a and
allenoate 2 a, in the presence of an L-V al-L-V al-based
dipeptide phosphonium salt catalyst P1 with using
cesium carbonate as base. The reaction proceeded
eff iciently in xylene at room temperature, and the
desired 4H-pyran product 3 a was obtained in high
yield (88%) with good diastereoselectivity (97:3), but
was almost racemic (T able 1, entry 1). In this context,
further optimization was mainly focusing on tuning the
catalyst skeletons. T o our gratification, the L-V al-D-
V al-based dipeptide phosphonium salt P2 afforded the
desired product 3 a in improved enantioselectivity
(18% ee, entry 2). Inspired by this preliminary result,
we then synthesized and examined a set of (L, D)-
dipeptide-based chiral phosphonium salts, and found
that both introduction of a bulky functionality such as
tert-butyldiphenylsilyl or tert-butyldimethylsilyl to
hydroxyl group and modification of alkyl halide with
sterically hindered aryl ring were benefical for the
stereocontrol of this reaction (entries 3–6). Among all,
the O-TBS-L-Thr -D-tert-Leu-based phosphonium salt
P6 was recognized as the most eff icient catalyst
(entry 6). For comparison, various amino-acid-derived
phosphonium salts with amides P7–P10 were also
screened under the aforementioned condition, and all
these amide-based catalyst gave the cyclized product
3 a in low to moderate ee values (entries 7–10).
Subsequently , the effects of solvent and base additives
were routinely conducted, and no better results were
obtained (T able S2 and T able S3).
[14a]
Additionally ,
when 4.0 equivalents of base Cs
2
CO
3
was applied, the
reaction time was shortened and the enantioselectivity
was slightly enhanced (entry 12). As expected, de-
creasing the reaction temperature to � 20 ° C could
improve the enantioselectivity for giving 96% ee

(entry 14). It is worth noting that the reactivity and
stereoselectivity were maintained even though a
10 mol% catalyst loading was employed (entry 15).
W ith the current optimized condition in hand
(T able 1, entry 15), the substrate scope of isoindigos
was investigated (T able 2). It was found that isoindigos
with N-Boc group bearing both electron-donating and
electron-withdrawing substituent groups on oxindole
moiety were well tolerated for this reaction, providing
relevant products 3 a–f in excellent yields, diastereo-
and enantioselectivities (up to 98% yield, > 20:1 dr
and up to 96% ee). When isoindigo 1 g with chloride
group at C4-position was used, the annulation product
3 g was not observed, probably due to the crowded
circumstance around the all-carbon quaternary center .
Unsymmetrical isoindigos were then evaluated. In the
perspective of synthetic methodology , isoindigos con-
taining oxindoles with dif ferent substituents are more
challenging, that usually lead to intricate regio-
isomeric products if the reaction is with a poor
regioselectivity .
[15]
Fortunately , the [4 + 2] annulation
of unsymmetrical isoindigos was precisely controlled
by our catalytic system, giving annulation products 3 h
and 3 i in regioselective and stereoselective manners.
Later , the substitution effects of allenoates 2 were
finally examined. The replacement of tert-butyl ester
or methyl group for allenoates with other substituents
had little influence on the reactivity and stereo-
selectivity , furnishing the products 3 j–l in 95–96%

yield with 91:9 to > 20:1 dr and 94–96% ee. More-
over , absolute configuration of 3 h was determined as
(3’S, 4S) by the X-ray analysis (see SI for details).
[16]
Whereafter , we turned our interest to the annulation
of allenoates 2 and pyrazoloneyldiene oxindoles 4 to
synthesize pyrano[2,3-c]-pyrazole derivatives 5, which
are structural analogues of potential drug candidates.
[17]
T o our delight, the reaction could also proceed
smoothly when we investigated the generality of
pyrazoloneyldiene oxindoles 4 with allenoates 2 after a
carefully systematic rescreening of catalyst.
[14b]
Of
note, high reactivities with good regioselectivities and
stereoselectivities were achieved under the reoptimized
condition (entry 3 in T able S9). In the presence of
10 mol% chiral phosphonium salt P10 and 4.0 equiv-
alent Cs
2
CO
3
, substrates 4 with dif ferent substituents
on the oxindole and pyrazolone moieties were inves-
tigated, furnishing the desired products 5 a–i in high
yields with good regio-, diastereo- and enantio-
selectivities (up to 96% yield, up to > 20:1 rr , 97:3 dr
and 97% ee). In addition, allenoates with benzyl and n-
butyl group were also allowed to react with pyrazolo-
neyldiene oxindole 4 a to aff ord regioselective and
stereoselective annulation products 5 j and 5 k respec-
tively . Finally , the relative and absolute configuration
of 5 c was determined as (3’S, 4S) by the X-ray
analysis (see SI for details).
[16]
In order to prove the eff ectiveness of this [4 + 2]
annulation reaction, we carried out the preparative
scaled synthesis of 3 h (Scheme 2a). It was gratifying
that both reactivity and stereoselectivities were main-
tained, for providing the desired product in 96% yield
with 92:8 dr and 90% ee. In addition, treatment of 3 h
with ferric chloride led to a selective hydrolysis
process and furnished the hydrolysed compound 6 in
good isolated yield with coincident stereoselectivities
(Scheme 2b).
Based on these results and our previous studies,
[9a–b]
a plausible reaction cycle was presented in Fig-
ure S3.
[14c]
T o demonstrate our hypothesis, the deute-
rium-labelling experiment was further conducted to get
preliminary supporting for this catalytic cycle. As
shown in Scheme 2c, when the model reaction was
performed in the presence of 10.0 equivalents of
additive D
2
O, deuterium incorporation into 3’-position
(30% D) of the cyclized product was observed, which

indicated the beneficial existence of possible inter-

Moreover , to gain some insights on vital stereo-control
mode of this transformation, we further prepared the
methylated catalyst P6–1 and P6–2 to view the
significance of H-bonding interactions for stereo-
induction. When either of methylated catalyst was used
for the model reaction, both diastereo- and enantio-
selectivities were decreased substantially (T able 4,
entries 1–3). Of note, when N-Methyl isoindigo was
employed, the corresponding product was isolated in
good yield but with a racemic version (entry 4), and
we guess that the N-Boc-protected isoindigo substrate
may be crucial for stereo-selectivity of the reaction.
However , when the model reaction was performed in
methanol, messy reaction was observed without for-
mation of any major products (entry 5), and we suspect
this may due to the instability of allene substrate under
slightly stronger basic system induced by polar solvent.
These experimental results indicated that the weak-
bond interactions including H-bonding and ion-pair
manners were critical for the excellent stereoselectiv-
ities under this bifunctional phosphonium catalysis,
and thus a plausible transition state model (TS1) was
proposed with respect to the key step of intermolecular
α-addition between allene 2 a and isoindigo 1 a.
In conclusion, we disclosed a highly efficient
phosphonium salt-catalyzed enantioselective [4 + 2]
annulation reaction between allenes and multi-substi-
tuted alkenones containing two identical/different
unsaturated heterocyclic moieties for the construction
of structurally fused and spirocyclic 4H-pyran core
frameworks. By employing an amino acid-derived
bifunctional phosphonium salt as phase-transfer cata-
lyst, a wide range of synthetically challenging, multi-
ply substituted and structurally fused heterocycles with
spiro-4H-pyran units were conveniently constructed in
high yields with excellent diastereo- and enantioselec-
tivities under mild conditions. In addition, this
annulation process is featured with very good regiose-
lectivities, and is highly useful for creating compli-
cated and challenging heterocyclic compounds. The
practicality and the utility of this protocol were
demonstrated by the scale-up synthetic reaction and
facile elaboration. Currently , further developments of
challenging asymmetric processes and their broadly
synthetic applications with such bifunctional
phosphonium salt catalysis are ongoing in our labo-
ratory .
